correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=4, marked singleton survival yields factorial moments \(\mathbb E(B_k)_r=(k)_r(k-1)_r/(n-1)_r\); merging two singles yields \(\mathbb EJ_j=(j-1)(j-2)/[(n-1)(n-2)]\). Split mixed moments at j<=k and j>k, subtract \(\mathbb EC_n\mathbb EB_k\), and telescope exactly to \(\operatorname{Cov}(C_n,B_k)=-k(k-1)(n-k)(n-k-1)/[3(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)]\). Independent holding times of mean \(2/[k(k-1)]\) then sum to \(-2/9\). For n=2,3 cherry count is deterministic. The packaged rational checker verifies exhaustive histories n=2..7, exact recursions through n=60 and 1,767 level checks, while the proof supplies all-n quantification.

originality.rationale: The candidate is the finite-n mixed cherry-count/total-external-length covariance, not either marginal distribution. Full-text checks of the external-length chain [1], cherry enumeration [2], richer joint ranked-tree state encoding [3], and coalescent covariance compendium [4], and François–Mioland (2007) separate cherry/length marginals [5] did not identify the exact level kernel or n-invariant \(-2/9\). A complete state encoding is potentially capable of computing it but does not itself state this evaluation. Unindexed historical mixed-generating-function treatment remains a documented risk.

value.rationale: Cherry count quantifies branching topology and external length quantifies singleton mutation opportunity; their association is a motivated joint genealogical observable. Negative covariance is sample-size-independent for every n>=4 and arises from a nontrivial cancellation of level-specific dependencies. The level-resolved kernel identifies which ancestral levels contribute and distinguishes the result from a marginal-moment recomputation. There is no claim of downstream theorem or independence.
